app.name: NetMaster
app.otherWindowTitle: The app is open in another window
app.otherWindowBody: Two windows writing progress would overwrite each other — so only one window learns at a time. Close the other one, or take over here.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: Your progress is safe on this device. Reloading usually fixes it; if it keeps happening, screenshot this and send it to the app author.

feedback.tier3Note: Read the solution, then type the answer yourself — typing it is how it sticks.

learn.title: Learn
learn.emptyBody: Part A modules will appear here. Each module follows your letter through the Internet's postal system.
learn.lessonLocked: Finish the previous lesson to unlock this one
learn.overdueBlockTitle: Your review box needs you first
learn.overdueBlockBody: Overdue backlog: {count}. Clear some of it before starting new lessons — well-timed review is what makes it stick.
learn.drillCardBody: 10 problems a day, against the clock — get fast with the magic number.
learn.challenge: I already know this — test out of it
learn.vmLabNoXp: Real-world work outside the app — it can't be verified, so no XP.
learn.streakFrozen: You skipped a stretch — {used} freeze(s) kept your streak alive ({left} left this month).
learn.streakReset: Your streak restarts today — those {lost} earlier days are still {lost} days you learned; nobody takes that away.

test.title: Module test
test.intro: {count} questions, {threshold}% needed to unlock the next module. No hints mid-test — this is where the knowledge stands on its own. Missing is fine: retake as many times as you like.
test.introFinal: {count} questions, {threshold}% needed to close out the whole course. No hints mid-test — this is where the knowledge stands on its own. Missing is fine: retake as many times as you like.
test.passTitleFinal: {pct}% — you just finished the final module of the course!
test.failBody: You need {threshold}% to unlock the next module. Read through the ideas below, then retake — retakes are for learning, not punishment.
test.failBodyFinal: You need {threshold}% to close out the course. Read through the ideas below, then retake — retakes are for learning, not punishment.
test.reviewHint: Review: {topic}. Revisit the lesson that teaches it, then retake — full answers appear once you pass.
test.reviewHintGeneric: Revisit the lesson that teaches this, then retake — full answers appear once you pass.
test.notReadyBody: Finish the lessons in this module first — the test draws on exactly that material.
test.challengeIntro: The same {count} questions as the end-of-module test, {threshold}% needed. Pass and this module counts as done and the next one opens — no sitting through material you already know.
test.challengeOneShot: Not passing costs you nothing: you can test out again straight away, or study it normally and take the end-of-module test like everyone else.
test.challengePass: {pct}% — you tested out, and the next module is unlocked!
test.challengePassFinal: {pct}% — you tested out of the final module, and that closes the whole course!
test.challengePassCards: This module's concepts just went into your review box, due tomorrow. Knowing it today is no promise you will recall it in three weeks — a few minutes of review a day is what keeps it.
test.challengeFailBody: Short of {threshold}%. You can test out again right away, though a couple of lessons from this module first would make it surer.

lesson.pretestIntro: Guess freely — this part is never scored.
lesson.orderHelp: Tap the lines in the order you think is correct.
lesson.selfExplainPassed: You explained it in your own words — that's how it really sticks!
lesson.notFound: This lesson could not be found.

review.title: Review
review.emptyBody: Finish your first lesson and the first card will schedule itself here — right before your brain lets it slip.
review.noneDueBody: Your cards are still "resting" — come back on {nextDate}. Spacing is the secret to remembering.
review.noneDueBodyNoDate: Your cards are still "resting" — come back later. Spacing is the secret to remembering.
review.selfGradeHint: Grade yourself honestly — cards you miss come back sooner to help you.
review.doneBody: You remembered {correct}/{total} cards. Missed cards return tomorrow.
review.whyHere: Cards due right now: {count}. Your brain is right on schedule to forget, so let's review first.

drill.title: Subnetting drill
drill.intro: 10 freshly generated problems a day, against the clock so your mental math speeds up. Mistakes are fine — the timer is only you racing yourself.
drill.qNetworkAddr: Find the network address of host {ip}/{prefix}.
drill.qBroadcast: Find the broadcast address of host {ip}/{prefix}.
drill.qHostRange: Host {ip}/{prefix}: find the first and last usable host (as "a - b").
drill.qHostCount: How many usable hosts does network {ip}/{prefix} have?
drill.qPrefixForHosts: You need room for {hosts} hosts — what is the smallest sufficient prefix (as /xx)?
drill.qMaskFromPrefix: Convert /{prefix} to a full subnet mask.
drill.qPrefixFromMask: Which prefix does subnet mask {mask} correspond to (as /xx)?
drill.backTomorrow: Come back tomorrow — steady practice is what builds speed.
drill.alreadyDoneToday: You already drilled today. Fancy one more round?

onboarding.invite: Before you learn a single thing — try sending a packet.
onboarding.deliveredBody: Your packet left Machine A, stopped by the router — the "mail carrier" read the address on the envelope and forwarded it — and landed at Machine B. This whole course is the story behind that trip.
onboarding.diagramAria: Network diagram: Machine A connects through a router to Machine B

lab.title: Network lab
lab.goalBlocked: {from} must NOT be able to reach {to}
lab.trayLocked: This task uses exactly the devices already on the bench.
lab.canvasAria: The network diagram you are building
lab.canvasEmpty: The bench is empty — add a device to begin.
lab.panelPick: Pick a device on the diagram to see and edit its settings.
lab.portPickTarget: Pick a free port to connect to {port}:
lab.sendFree: Try as many times as you like — this part is never scored.
lab.submitHint: Only submitting counts as an attempt. Experiment first, submit when you're ready.
lab.hopEmpty: Press "Try it" to watch a packet travel through your diagram.
lab.reasonBroadcastFlood: asking the whole network — who holds this address?
lab.reasonUnknownUnicastFlood: the switch doesn't know which port yet, so it sends to all of them
lab.reasonMacTableHit: the switch remembers the destination and sends out exactly one port
lab.reasonRouted: router forwards it — new hardware address, same IP address
lab.resultOk: The packet arrived and a reply came back.
lab.resultReachedOnly: The packet arrived, but there is no way back for the reply.
lab.resultFail: The packet never reached its destination.

failure.src-not-found: The sending machine could not be found.
failure.dst-not-found: The receiving machine could not be found.
failure.src-no-ip: The sender has no IP address yet.
failure.dst-no-ip: The receiver has no IP address yet.
failure.src-no-link: The sender isn't plugged into anything.
failure.no-gateway: The destination is outside the local range and the sender has no way out (gateway).
failure.gateway-off-subnet: The gateway address isn't in the machine's own range, so it can't be reached.
failure.arp-unresolved: The sender asked "who holds this address?" and nobody answered.
failure.no-route: The router has no path towards that address range.
failure.hop-budget-exceeded: The packet kept bouncing between routers without arriving.
failure.broadcast-storm: The network has a loop: the broadcast came back to where it started and multiplied.

diagnosis.device-isolated: A device isn't plugged into anything.
diagnosis.missing-ip: A machine has no IP address set.
diagnosis.missing-gateway: A machine needs to talk outside its own range but has no gateway.
diagnosis.gateway-not-in-subnet: The gateway isn't in the same range as the machine's address.
diagnosis.duplicate-ip: Two devices carry the same IP address.
diagnosis.vlan-mismatch-on-link: A cable joins two ports that sit in different VLANs.
diagnosis.same-subnet-different-vlan: Two machines share an address range but sit in different VLANs.
diagnosis.l2-loop: The diagram has a loop between switches.

refusal.not-allowed: This task doesn't let you change that — try another angle.
refusal.max-devices: The bench already has all the devices this task needs.
refusal.duplicate-device-id: A device with that name is already on the bench.
refusal.unknown-device: That device could not be found.
refusal.unknown-port: That port could not be found.
refusal.unknown-link: That cable could not be found.
refusal.wrong-device-kind: This device doesn't have that setting.
refusal.port-occupied: This port already has a cable — remove the old one first.
refusal.self-link: A cable needs to join two different devices.
refusal.invalid-vlan: A VLAN number must be between 1 and 4094.
refusal.invalid-ip: An IP address looks like four groups of digits, e.g. 192.168.1.10.
refusal.invalid-prefix: The prefix must be between 0 and 32.

lab.narrowTitle: The lab wants a wider screen
lab.narrowBody: Everything still works through the configuration panel below — only the diagram gets smaller.

flow.harderNote: You're on a roll — try typing the answer for this one instead of picking.
flow.supportTitle: Let's pick up a few foundation bricks first
flow.supportBody: The last stretch was bumpy — that's perfectly normal. We'll glance back at a few concepts this lesson stands on: try to recall before you flip, then climb right on.

palace.tourCompleted: You've walked this stretch — in a moment we'll walk it again from memory.
palace.cueAria: The memory image of this room
palace.walkPrompt: You're standing at this door. What's inside?
palace.missingRooms: Couldn't load the building for this walk.
palace.tourGate: Walk this stretch to the end and we'll move on — in a moment you'll walk it again from memory.

clinic.title: Clinic
clinic.lockedBody: Behind this door are real "patients": unplugged cables, a silent DNS, a gateway with the wrong address… You'll play the diagnostician — but the foundation modules come first. Keep learning; the clinic opens itself when you're ready.
clinic.seatLine: You're sitting at the patient's machine {host}. No diagram yet — every clue comes from the terminal below, just like a real on-call shift.
clinic.terminalIntro: Type commands to examine the patient — start with help if you're unsure. Examining is always free.
clinic.terminalPlaceholder: Type a command… (help lists them all)
clinic.termUnknown: This machine has no "{cmd}" command — type help to see the list.
clinic.termCaptureEmpty: No packets captured yet — run ping or tracert first, then capture will have a story to tell.

cmd.ipconfig: show this machine's IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DNS
cmd.ping: send probe packets to an address or name — ping <target>
cmd.tracert: show the router-by-router path to a target — tracert <target>
cmd.nslookup: ask DNS what address a name points to — nslookup <name>
cmd.netstat: list the network connections open on this machine
cmd.arp: show the IP-to-MAC table (ARP cache) this machine has resolved
cmd.capture: show the packet capture of the latest ping/tracert (a tiny Wireshark)
cmd.gpresult: list the Group Policy Objects applied to this machine

clinic.diagnosisHint: Examine through the terminal first — name the illness, then you get to fix it.
clinic.fixIntroEdit: Your turn now: here is the patient's diagram — fix it directly.
clinic.fixIntroAction: This illness can't be fixed from where you sit — pick the best course of action.
clinic.symptomStillSick: The patient still shows the original symptom — not cured yet.
clinic.symptomCleared: The original symptom is gone — submit when you're confident.
clinic.listIntro: Every patient you met in Module 11 stays admitted here — re-examine them as often as you like, with the same 3-tier hint ladder.
clinic.listXpNote: XP is awarded only for the first cure of each case
clinic.firstSolveXp: +{xp} XP — this case is now in your casebook.
clinic.resolveNoXp: You've already cured this one — no XP this time, but the practice counts.

ps.terminalIntro: Type commands to work the task — Get-Help lists the toolbox if you forget. Trying is always free.
ps.terminalPlaceholder: Type a PowerShell command… (Get-Help lists them)
ps.termUnknown: This machine has no "{cmd}" cmdlet — type Get-Help to see the list.

cmd.Get-NetIPAddress: show the IP addresses of this machine's network cards
cmd.Test-NetConnection: test ping or a TCP port to a target — Test-NetConnection <target> [-Port <n>]
cmd.New-ADUser: create a new user — -Name, -SamAccountName, -Path; or accept bulk rows from the pipe
cmd.Import-Csv: read a CSV file into records — pipeable
cmd.Get-Content: read a file line by line
cmd.Select-String: filter lines containing a phrase — Select-String <phrase> [<file>]

ps.termCreatedSilent: (the command finished silently, just like real PowerShell — created {count} user(s); run Get-ADUser to see for yourself)
ps.goalAdUserCount: The {ou} OU must have at least {atLeast} users
ps.goalFoundLine: Pulled out a log line containing "{text}"
ps.freeNote: Typing and starting over are free — only "Submit" counts as an attempt.

profile.title: Profile
profile.emptyBadges: Badges are coming in a later version — your XP, streak and every case you cure are all being recorded.
profile.freezeNote: Missing a day won't break your streak — you get 2 automatic "freezes" each month.
profile.backupBody: Progress lives in this device's browser — clearing browsing data or switching machines loses it. Export a file now and then; import it on a new machine to pick up where you left off.
profile.backupImportConfirm: Importing will REPLACE all progress on this device with the file's progress. Continue?
profile.backupImportBad: That file is not a valid NetMaster backup — double-check you picked the right one.
